text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created at 1798123456 — gpool-prod experiencing sustained queue growth and autoscaler failing to add nodes. Severity: P1.

maya: seeing large queue backlog on gpool-prod, requests/sec flat but pending tasks climbing. autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts hitting limit.

oliver: checking autoscaler — it's hitting the per-cluster instance limit (max_instances=120). we're at 118, attempts to add 4 nodes failing with quota error in cloud API.

dave: runtime reports lots of CUDA Xid errors on several nodes, driver restarts in last 30m. effective GPU capacity lower than reported. suspect kernel/driver instability causing nodes to flail and autoscaler to avoid adding replacements.

lina: support-bot alerted two customers (search-app-prod, recs-engine) reporting higher latencies and 429s. I've opened tickets and flagged major-impact.

maya: quick ask: can we throttle low-priority tenants and enable model-fallback to smaller variants? need mitigation to reduce queue.

oliver: we can push a temporary admission-control patch to router to reject non-production namespaces (rate-limit) — rolling deploy to edge in ~5m.

dave: for driver noise: logs show repeated OOMs in nvidia-driver module after long-running KV cache usage. sample: ```
[2026-07-21T03:12:10Z] nvidia: GPU 2: Xid 79, process 0x1234f
[2026-07-21T03:12:12Z] oom_kill_process: Out of memory: Killed process 2421 (runtime) total-vm: 123456kB
```

maya: timeline — queue started rising at ~1798121000, spike after 1798122000 when a nightly large-batch job from analytics ran. autoscaler attempted to scale at ~1798122500 and again at ~1798123200 but cloud API returned quota error.

oliver: cloud quota team contacted — they're provisioning a short-lived bump but ETA ~30m. in the meantime we should free capacity: evict best-effort / spot workloads, cordon nodes with noisy drivers.

dave: plan to cycle drivers on 3 noisy nodes (gpu-node-37, 41, 45). I'll trigger driver reloads and monitor Xid rates. If driver reloads don't stick, we'll move pods off those nodes.

lina: notifying impacted customers: search-app-prod sees p95 latency from 120ms -> 1.4s; recs-engine request timeouts for some batched endpoints. customers asked for ETA and mitigation.

maya: execute mitigations now: 1) admission control deploy (oliver) 2) throttle low-priority routes (maya) 3) cordon noisy nodes (oliver) 4) restart drivers (dave) 5) enable fallback model variants for heavy callers (prod-config) 6) escalate quota (oliver). keep updates here.

oliver: deploying admission control patch — will route non-prod to 429 with Retry-After. rolling across edge fleet. patch diff: ```yaml
routes:
  - match: /v1/embed
    namespace_allowlist: [prod]
```

dave: starting driver reload on gpu-node-37 via runbook step: `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service` and watch dmesg. tailing: ```
Jul 21 03:20:10 gpu-node-37 kernel: nvidia: driver reloaded
Jul 21 03:20:11 gpu-node-37 kernel: GPU 2: Xid 79 count down
```

maya: admission control is active — seeing drop in new queued entries from non-prod namespaces. queue growth rate reduced ~30%.

oliver: cordoned gpu-node-41 and 45, evicting spot pods; autoscaler should be able to schedule replacements once quota bump arrives.

dave: driver reloads reduced Xid rate on node-37, but node-45 still flaps. preparing to drain 45 and move persistent pods to new nodes.

lina: updated customers: ETA for capacity relief ~30-45m once quota bump lands; temporary throttles are in place. customer replies: search-app-prod asked for a more aggressive fallback; enabling smaller model now.

support-bot: customer-impact: search-app-prod (P1) degraded p95 latency, recs-engine (P2) increased timeouts. tickets #2342 and #2389 updated.

omnicorp-benchmark-bot: load test spike correlates with analytics nightly job at 1798122000, marking correlation.

maya: cloud quota team just confirmed a 20-instance soft increase  — will unblock autoscaler. oliver, once confirmed, please uncordon as capacity stabilizes.

oliver: quota increase applied at 1798126200. autoscaler immediately scheduled 6 new nodes but some failed to register because runtime agent on the new nodes is failing TLS handshake — investigating.

dave: runtime agent errors on new nodes show `KV cache warmup` timeout causing agent to crash on first model load. stack: `runtime -> model-loader -> kvcache` ; will patch to skip warmup on first boot. work-in-progress, ETA 20m.

maya: interim: continue draining flappy nodes, keep throttles, and rely on fallback variants for heavy tenants. need a short blameless RCA after incident: root cause seems to be interplay of driver instability reducing effective capacity + autoscaler hitting hard limits.

oliver: I'm going to scale down best-effort pools to free GPU slots for production; will post completed when done.

dave: patched agent on one new node manually and it registered fine. rolling manual patch to remaining launching nodes to speed registration.

lina: customers acknowledged mitigations and appreciate frequent updates; search-app-prod wants a postmortem and SLA credit evaluation. logging that.

sre-bridge-bot: maya is handing off to night-oncall (oliver) at 1798128200 — please continue monitoring and post a final incident summary when stable.

maya: handing off — summary: queue growth due to analytics spike + driver-induced capacity loss. mitigations executed: admission control, cordon/drain noisy nodes, driver restarts, temporary quota bump, throttle low-priority tenants, enable fallback models. Current status: queue decelerating, autoscaler adding nodes; some runtime agent instability on new nodes being fixed.

oliver: acknowledged. will monitor 4hr burn and coordinate postmortem with dave and lina. I'll also follow up with cloud quota team and infra to set higher safety margins for autoscaler.

dave: will collect driver and runtime logs, reproduce OOM pattern in staging. probable fixes: disable aggressive KV warmup, bump kernel module retry, and add guardrails on nightly analytics batches.

lina: I'll prepare customer communication and timeline; will include mitigation summary and next steps for SLA review.

sre-bridge-bot: incident marked mitigated at 1798129430. please file postmortem and tag incident ID INC-2026-07-21-gpool for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
